correctness.rationale: The sum of i^m for 0≤i<n is interpolated by expanding i^m in falling factorials and summing them, with coefficients of denominator at most p^floor(log_p(m+1)) in p-adic valuation. Each m≥1 term of the geometric/binomial expansion for H_s, s=1,2, therefore has coefficient valuations at least m−floor(log_p(m+1))≥1, tending to infinity, including at p=3. This proves actual restricted-series convergence with H_s=x/c^s modulo p on coefficients. Newton's identity gives F=x(x−1)/(2c²)+pR. By density this is the unique continuous, hence unique analytic, interpolation. The map x−c²F′(x) is a contraction since R′ is integral restricted, giving the unique critical point α reducing to 1/2; substituting gives the stated unit critical value modulo p. Translating by α makes the difference from A into z² times a restricted analytic unit congruent to (2c²)⁻¹ on coefficients. The binomial square root of that unit after scaling by 2c² is in 1+p times the restricted algebra, since 1/2 is p-adic integral. Thus the normalized critical coordinate is z+pV(z), an isometry onto by contraction. This preserves uniform residue classes and gives the exact root counts, attainable residues and shell measure. For a nonzero shift t with v_p(t)<k the first factor in the difference of the squares has valuation v_p(t); modulo p the sum factor is 2(x−α)+t and can be made a unit by choosing an integer x. This proves the exact p^k period and the asserted densities.
residual_risks: The finite replay checks the distribution's shape about the observed center, not the analytic construction or the critical center at unlimited precision. Those follow from the restricted-series proof. There is no assertion when p divides a denominator or p=2.

originality.rationale: The underlying elementary symmetric sums are known. The supported distinct claim is the global isometric square normal form for the regular primes dividing the progression step, with all modular fibers, periods and density. The strongest inspected exact-sequence literature treats integrality, and the strongest indexed square-image analogues concern different functions. General Morse normal forms and quadratic residue counts are not credited as new. This is a bounded evidence judgment, not a claim of demonstrated priority.
residual_risks: Priority against unindexed specializations of nonarchimedean normal forms or inaccessible related work has not been settled. No noncoverage finding is inferred from access failures.

value.rationale: The theorem describes the entire local distribution of a known arithmetic sequence in the unit-denominator regime where integrality results do not resolve it. The global analytic square coordinate is useful on its own: it gives one explicit obstruction at every precision, with exact densities, and the proof works uniformly even at the smallest odd prime. The square-root counts alone are routine, but obtaining the uniform global analytic shape from reciprocal progression sums is substantive.
residual_risks: The critical value is given analytically and need not have a simple rational expression. The result is not an integrality theorem outside the unit-denominator regime.
